decision.explanation: The characteristic polynomial is (λ−3)((λ−1)^2+1), so A has eigenvalues 3 and 1±i. The conjugate pair gives the rotation-scaling block [[1,1],[-1,1]], while the real eigenvalue gives the block [3]. Thus option b is the required real block diagonal form.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3-\lambda  & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =1\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 3-\lambda  & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =1\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

before.name: Question 2
before.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} \\ 5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 3-\text{i} \\ -5+2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=\text{i}+5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[1−i2+i5i2−i],v3=[3+2i1−i3−i−5+2i],B=[2−1001200005100−15] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=2−i and λ3=i+5, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[321−11−1213−105−522−1]
b
[−1132121−1503−1−12−52]
c
[1−132211−1053−12−1−52]
d
[23−11−1112−13502−5−12]
e
[1−12321−1105−132−12−5]

decision.explanation: For an eigenvector v=u+iw with eigenvalue a+bi, columns [u,w] produce the block [[a,b],[-b,a]]. Thus P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),Re(v₃),Im(v₃)], matching the blocks for 2−i and 5+i. These columns give option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} \\ 5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 3-\text{i} \\ -5+2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=\text{i}+5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[321−11−1213−105−522−1]
b
[−1132121−1503−1−12−52]
c
[1−132211−1053−12−1−52]
d
[23−11−1112−13502−5−12]
e
[1−12321−1105−132−12−5]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[2−1001200005100−15], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[1−132211−1053−12−1−52].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} \\ 5\text{i} \\ 2-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 3-\text{i} \\ -5+2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=\text{i}+5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: For an eigenvector v=u+iw with eigenvalue a+bi, the columns [u,w] give the block [[a,b],[-b,a]]. Both blocks of B match the stated eigenvalues, so P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),Re(v₃),Im(v₃)]. Taking these real and imaginary parts gives option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+4\text{i} \\ 3+7\text{i} \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3+2\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1+2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3-2\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 7 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+4\text{i} \\ 3+7\text{i} \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3+2\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1+2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3-2\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 7 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: The rotation-scaling block for 2+8i requires the columns Re(v₁)=(3,1,0)ᵀ and Im(v₁)=(5,−6,4)ᵀ. The final column is v₃=(5,2,1)ᵀ for eigenvalue −5. Therefore P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),v₃], which is option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2+8\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3+5i1−6i4i],v3=[521],B=[280−82000−5] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=2+8i and λ3=−5, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[3551−62041]
b
[325162140]
c
[3532−6001−4]
d
[3515−65046]
e
[552102−641]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[280−82000−5], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[3551−62041]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2+8\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[2−5i3i−8],v3=[23−1],B=[610−160002] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=6+i and λ3=2, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[1−52023−84−1]
b
[2−52033−80−1]
c
[2−52303−40−1]
d
[2−13032−805]
e
[2−521−33−801]
Submit

decision.explanation: The block [[6,1],[-1,6]] requires columns Re(v₁)=(2,0,−8)ᵀ and Im(v₁)=(−5,3,0)ᵀ. The third column is v₃=(2,3,−1)ᵀ. Thus P=[Re(v₁),Im(v₁),v₃], exactly option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2-5\text{i} \\ 3\text{i} \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=6+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 \\ -8 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 5

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[2−5i3i−8],v3=[23−1],B=[610−160002] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=6+i and λ3=2, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[1−52023−84−1]
b
[2−52033−80−1]
c
[2−52303−40−1]
d
[2−13032−805]
e
[2−521−33−801]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[610−160002], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[2−52033−80−1]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2-5\text{i} \\ 3\text{i} \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=6+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 \\ -8 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
